recent_posts.title: Chromium Blog: JetStream 3: A modern benchmark for high-performance, compute-intensive Web applications
recent_posts.summary: JetStream 3 is a new browser benchmark developed collaboratively by Google, Apple, Mozilla, and other partners, replacing JetStream 2 from 2019. It focuses on computationally intensive web workloads including browser games, physics simulations, cryptography, and complex algorithms. A major update is the expanded WebAssembly coverage: 12 new Wasm workloads now cover toolchains including Rust, Kotlin/Wasm, Dart2wasm, J2CL, and .NET, with Wasm making up 15-20% of the suite (up from 7%). New JavaScript workloads cover real-world use cases like React SSR, TypeScript compilation, Babylon.js, Three.js, and MobX startup performance. The benchmark is designed to run in engine shells like V8's d8 for faster iteration, and uses a consensus governance model across all major browser vendors.

recent_posts.title: Chromium Blog: Android Sets New Record for Mobile Web Performance
recent_posts.summary: Google announces that Android is now the fastest mobile platform for web browsing, setting new records in the Speedometer and LoadLine benchmarks with Chrome 146. The achievement results from deep vertical integration across hardware, Android OS, and the Chrome engine. LoadLine, a new end-to-end benchmark developed with SoC and OEM partners, shows top Android phones scoring up to 47% higher than non-Android competitors on page load performance. Year-over-year, flagship Android phones improved Speedometer and LoadLine scores by 20-60%, translating to 4-6% faster page loads and 6-9% faster high-percentile interactions for real users.

recent_posts.title: Chromium Blog: Bringing Chrome to ARM64 Linux Devices
recent_posts.summary: Google has announced the launch of Chrome for ARM64 Linux devices in Q2 2026, extending its browser support following earlier releases for Arm-powered macOS (2020) and Windows (2024). The release brings full Google ecosystem integration including sync, Chrome Web Store access, Safe Browsing with AI-powered Enhanced Protection, Google Pay, and Password Manager to ARM64 Linux users. Google is partnering with NVIDIA to streamline Chrome installation on the DGX Spark AI supercomputing device, while other Linux distributions can install it via chrome.com/download.

recent_posts.title: Chromium Blog: Reducing notification overload for a quieter browsing experience in Chrome
recent_posts.summary: Chrome is introducing automatic revocation of notification permissions for sites with low user engagement and high notification volume. The feature, rolling out on Android and desktop, uses Safety Check to remove permissions from sites users haven't interacted with recently, while preserving notifications for installed web apps. Testing shows significant reduction in notification overload with minimal impact on engagement, and users can easily re-grant permissions or disable the feature entirely.

recent_posts.title: Chromium Blog: Introducing Skia Graphite: Chrome's rasterization backend for the future
recent_posts.summary: Chrome has launched Skia Graphite, a new GPU rasterization backend that replaces the older Ganesh system. Graphite delivers 15% better Motionmark 1.3 scores on Apple Silicon Macs while improving real-world metrics like interaction timing and graphics smoothness. The new backend leverages modern graphics APIs through WebGPU Dawn, implements 2D depth testing to reduce overdraw, and supports multithreading by design. Unlike Ganesh's specialized shader approach, Graphite consolidates rendering pipelines to prevent performance cliffs and compilation jank. Future plans include multithreaded rasterization, reduced GPU memory usage for simple content, and GPU compute-based path rasterization.

recent_posts.title: Chrome achieves record Speedometer 3 performance with 10% improvement
recent_posts.summary: Chrome achieved its highest Speedometer 3 benchmark score with a 10% performance improvement since August 2024, potentially saving users 58 million hours collectively. The improvements came from optimizing memory layouts across DOM, CSS, layout and painting components, enhancing string handling with better hashing algorithms, improving cache utilization for CSS style computation, and significantly boosting font shaping performance. These optimizations target the entire rendering pipeline including HTML parsing, JavaScript processing, DOM manipulation, and pixel rendering.

recent_posts.title: Chromium Blog: Fighting Unwanted Notifications with Machine Learning in Chrome
recent_posts.summary: Chrome is enhancing user safety by launching a new feature that uses machine learning on Android devices to identify and warn users about spammy or deceptive notifications. This on-device model examines the contents of notifications, offering users options to unsubscribe or view flagged content. Notifications remain encrypted for privacy, with the model trained on synthetic data from the Gemini large language model.

recent_posts.title: Chromium Blog: Announcing Supporters of Chromium-based Browsers
recent_posts.summary: Google announces a partnership with The Linux Foundation to launch the Supporters of Chromium-based Browsers fund. The initiative aims to promote a sustainable environment for the development of the Chromium ecosystem, with initial backing from Meta, Microsoft, and Opera. Google highlights its continued significant investment in the project's maintenance and future advancements.

recent_posts.title: Chromium Blog: Making Chrome QUICer
recent_posts.summary: Chrome has enabled HTTP/3 by default since October 2020, resulting in improved performance including reduced Google search latency and fewer YouTube rebuffers. Recent updates in Chrome include the implementation of the HTTP/3 ORIGIN frame and Server's Preferred Address, which enhance connection coalescing and reduce round trip time (RTT) respectively. These features were introduced in M131, released to Stable on November 19. The ORIGIN frame helps pool domains onto a connection, while Server's Preferred Address allows migration to a more efficient server route, significantly lowering RTT.

recent_posts.title: Chromium Blog: How Chrome doubled its Speedometer scores on Android
recent_posts.summary: Chrome has achieved significant improvements in its Speedometer performance scores on Android devices, doubling them in many cases. This was accomplished through build optimizations, enhancements to the V8 and Blink engines, and close collaboration with Android hardware partners. These changes translate to faster page loads and smoother interactions for users.
